newsitem.title: DUBAI: Indian child beggars to leave Saudi on Sunday. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT, 02/02/97]
newsitem.headline: Indian child beggars to leave Saudi on Sunday. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT, 02/02/97]

text.p: The Indian consulate has finalised issuing travel papers to 46 Indian children awaiting deportation from Saudi Arabia after being caught begging, an Indian diplomat said on Saturday.
"All 46 children have been issued travel documents...They will leave Saudi Arabia on an Air India flight to Bombay on Sunday," the diplomat told Reuters by telephone from Saudi Arabia.
"We hope to be able to get all of them on one flight," he added.

The 40 boys and six girls, aged between six and 14, appeared to have entered Saudi Arabia, known for tough visa laws, as Moslem pilgrims in families. When relatives returned to India they stayed behind as beggars.

They were caught this month pleading for food and money in the streets of Mecca and Medina, home to two of Islam's holiest shrines, and were taken to the deportation centre in nearby Jeddah without identification papers.
"When they arrive home they will be handed over to their families, they have not violated any Indian law as far as we are concerned," the diplomat said.
They would be the second batch of Indian children deported by Saudi Arabia in less than a month for staying illegally in the oil-rich country and earning their living as beggars.
At least 76 girls aged between five and 14, many handicapped, were deported to Bombay on January 13.
